extracted.intended_audience: authors/researchers preparing revisions and responses to journal peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on how to prepare a response letter and revise a manuscript after receiving peer review decisions (minor/major revisions, rejection). Covers what to include in responses, how to handle disagreements or conflicting reviews, and revision strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper accepted without any revisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the decision type; indicates acceptance as-is is uncommon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted pending minor revisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the kinds of changes typically requested for this decision and that the revisions are expected to be limited in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted pending major revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Usually includes dataset or methodology revisions and/or major rewriting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals that substantial changes to methods, data, or narrative are expected; may require substantial time and effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejected without external review
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates paper is outside journal scope or did not meet standards of a very prestigious journal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains one reason for editorial rejection prior to sending to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejected after external review
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible major deficiencies in paper or poor writing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that review-led rejection often reflects important problems in the manuscript that should be addressed before resubmission elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address every reviewer comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Every comment from each reviewer needs to be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not ignore reviewer points; failure to respond to comments can result in rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a response letter/document with revised manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: A response letter or document should be included with your revised manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This document should list all the points made by reviewers and how you addressed them. Use it to make the editor/reviewers’ job easier.

rubrics_metrics.name: List reviewer points and explain how each was addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: This document should list all the points made by reviewers and how you addresses them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a point-by-point mapping between reviewer comments and the corresponding changes or rebuttals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight changes in the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: You should also highlight the changes made in your manuscript, so they are easily discoverable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use highlighting, tracked changes, or a changelog so editors/reviewers can quickly find revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polite rebuttal with documentation when disagreeing
rubrics_metrics.description: If you strongly disagree with a comment and decide to keep that portion of the manuscript the same, write a polite rebuttal with documentation to support your position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why you are retaining the text/approach and back it up with evidence, citations, or rationale rather than dismissing the reviewer brusquely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set major revision request aside briefly before starting
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are asked to make major revisions, ... set the revision request aside for a short period of time and then go back to it with a clear head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taking a short break can help manage frustration and allow a clearer, more strategic revision plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be flexible and view reviewers as helping improve the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Be flexible and understand that reviewers are trying to help you in ending up with a well-written and methodologically strong paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a collaborative mindset; consider reviewers' suggestions seriously even if they require substantial change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise the entire manuscript for flow, not just flagged sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire manuscript, not just specific sections pointed out, should be revised to ensure a good flow throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use revision as an opportunity to improve coherence and consistency across the whole paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be honest when you cannot comply and update Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are unable to revise the manuscript as suggested by a reviewer's comment, be honest in your response to the reviewers about why you are not able to correct the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise the Limitations section of your manuscript to include the issue that you are unable to rectify, and explain constraints in your response letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact the editor if a reviewer misunderstood you
rubrics_metrics.description: If you or your team believes that a reviewer has misunderstood you, politely contact the journal editor and explain your perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the editor as an intermediary to clarify misunderstandings rather than confronting reviewers directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve conflicting reviewer comments via editor or reasoned choice
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a conflict between reviewer comments, contact the editor and ask how this conflict might best be resolved. If the comments by different reviewers are pertinent but conflicting, it is up to your team to choose which commentary to use in moving forward with your revisions (explaining why that particular path was chosen over another).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either seek editor guidance or select one path and justify the decision clearly in your response letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address peer review comments after rejection before resubmitting
rubrics_metrics.description: If your article was rejected after peer review, take the time to address the peer reviewers comments before you submit to another journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporating reviewer feedback can strengthen the manuscript and improve chances of acceptance upon resubmission elsewhere.
